video_title: Mahershala Ali Gets Real on Blade, Why 2 Oscars Don't Guarantee Roles & Ranks GOAT Hoop Films

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on Steph Curry finishing his career with the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: I would love for him to stay and I would love for him to do something like what Magic and Larry Bird did.
quotes.quote: I would hope we could have both. But I'm a fan, so I don't know how realistic fans are all the time. But at the end of the day, if Steph wants to be there, I would love for him to stay and I would love for him to do something like what Magic and Larry Bird did, some of those brothers who were able to stay with the team and be defined by that in some ways. But at this point, clearly Steph has earned the right to do whatever he wants to do. He doesn't owe us anything per se, but it's been beautiful getting to watch his career unfold and play out. I was really worried early on with all the ankle injuries and what not. You weren't sure if we were going to have him on the court like that, but considering he was able to get past that and be relatively healthy for years, yeah, I would love to see him stay.
quotes.social_post: Mahershala Ali on Steph Curry: I would love for him to stay with the Warriors and be defined by that in some ways, like Magic and Larry Bird. He has earned the right to do whatever he wants to do.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on how NIL and COVID changed college basketball
quotes.excerpt: I think COVID, even maybe even more than the NIL, has really shifted college sports in terms of the eligibility.
quotes.quote: I think we're in a very different time and we're still trying to acclimate in terms of how to think about it. I think COVID, even maybe even more than the NIL, has really shifted college sports in terms of the eligibility factors that weighed in where therefore kids coming out of high school or even JC are having a more difficult time getting scholarships now. People being able to stay longer because now they're getting paid to be in school. So I think between the combination of COVID and the NIL opportunities, it's made college basketball even more competitive in terms of the spots. I think the thing that college had going for it is the very thing that a lot of us would call BS, but it also is what college ball had going for it in terms of camaraderie and doing it for something bigger than yourself, learning about sacrifice, the pride, loving the school, your teammates and what not, before you end up getting hit with all the, this is how you take care of yourself and this is how you become the best player, this is how you have longevity and all that.
quotes.social_post: Mahershala Ali says the combination of NIL and COVID has made college basketball even more competitive for roster spots and shifted the traditional culture of the game.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali reflects on his difficult experience playing at St. Mary's
quotes.excerpt: I think because of hitting that wall, sort of beginning to lose the love of the game.
quotes.quote: I wanted to transfer. So I was at St. Mary's and by after my sophomore year, I definitely wanted to transfer. And I'm glad I didn't, because I ended up who you are today. It's also just like I think because of hitting that wall, sort of beginning to lose the love of the game at that time, because I think I was so turned off by the business of it.
quotes.social_post: Mahershala Ali reflects on his college playing days at St. Marys, admitting he almost transferred after his sophomore year because he was losing his love for the game.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Ali felt his coach viewed players as disposable stepping stones
quotes.excerpt: I could tell that there was a stepping stone quality to my coach's presence.
quotes.quote: I could tell that there was a stepping stone quality to my coach's presence. Like he wanted to win so he could go to Oregon. He was out as soon as they went to the tournament the year after I graduated and next you know, he was at Oregon. He didn't say this, but just in terms of how he treated players, that the player that he recruited, if you didn't just magically make that leap, then he almost didn't feel like you were worthy. He couldn't coach you up. He wasn't going to help you and you kind of had to just come ready made. Otherwise, I'm going to find just another recruit.
quotes.social_post: Mahershala Ali opens up about his college coach, saying he felt like a disposable stepping stone for the coach to land a bigger job at Oregon.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Disappointment in the lack of a fatherly coaching relationship
quotes.excerpt: I didn't really play for Black coaches coming up. So I think I had in my mind.
quotes.quote: I didn't really play for Black coaches coming up. So I think I had in my mind this element of almost like a fatherly figure as a coach. And like almost like a John Thompson, you're thinking like you're going to have a certain type of relationship where he's going to look out for me in a different way. And if anything, it was the opposite. It was the opposite.
quotes.social_post: Mahershala Ali shares his disappointment in his college coaching experience, noting he hoped for a fatherly figure like John Thompson but found the opposite.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony on the importance of cooking steak to the right temperature
quotes.excerpt: Well-done steak is overhead. I've killed some for reasons.

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: Well-done steak is overhead. I've killed some for reasons.

text_blocks.speaker: The Kid Mero
text_blocks.text: Not your reasons. You go to a Peruvian spot, them Colombians, they cook all their steaks on one temperature. You ask steak, it's medium.

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: They give you skirt steak. You say medium, they be like, yeah, yeah, yeah, medium. Skirt steak.

text_blocks.speaker: The Kid Mero
text_blocks.text: They only got the skirt steak, okay? They got no temperatures.

quotes.social_post: Carmelo Anthony weighs in on the steak debate, defending well-done steak and discussing the realities of ordering at different restaurants.

quotes.speaker: The Kid Mero
quotes.summary_phrase: The Kid Mero praises Carmelo Anthony's intentionality and artistic journey
quotes.excerpt: It's beautiful to have this type of energy in somebody who is as intentional and grounded as yourself.

text_blocks.speaker: The Kid Mero
text_blocks.text: It's beautiful to have this type of energy in somebody who is as intentional and grounded as yourself. As a fan of your art and just your journey, and saw the type of scripts that you take that sometimes can be traditional, but expected, and you turn that into magic and you turn that into art to where we become fans of you.

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: Brother, thank you. I appreciate that, man. I just want to give you your flowers. A lot of times we give flowers to people that's dead.

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: I appreciate you, brother. It means a lot coming from you, really.

quotes.social_post: The Kid Mero gives Carmelo Anthony his flowers, praising his intentionality and the way he turns his work into art.
